proof_steps.text: Filtration and radical. For $n=0$ there is one empty multipartition, $S_{\mathcal O}=\mathcal O$, $\Delta_{\mathcal O}=\mathcal O$ with form $1$, every positive filtration term is $0$, and every $J$ coefficient is $0$, so the assertions follow directly. For $n\ge1$, [F1] gives free standard lattices with nondegenerate generic forms. The Smith reduction of [F4] shows that the defined filtration is by $S_F$-submodules, begins at $\Delta_F(\lambda)$, has first term equal to the form radical, and is zero for all sufficiently large $s$. The rank-one cell actions of the nonzero cellular form force every proper submodule into that radical, so the first term is the module radical. [given, F1, F4]

The auxiliary character identity. Introduce ordered variables for the type-row labels; the auxiliary generating series of flagged semistandard tableaux is the product over physical components $a$ of $s_{\lambda^{(a)}}(Y_a)$, where $Y_a$ is the alphabet of type components at least $a$, and its coefficient at an actual multipartition $\nu$ is $K_{\lambda\nu}$. Successive $\Gamma_a$ matrices add the horizontal strips carrying each next label and therefore enumerate these tableaux once; the path/Jacobi–Trudi cancellation proves this character identity locally. No actual Schur weight or module for another composition is needed. [F1, F3]

The weight-character reduction. Fix an actual multipartition weight $
u$. The selfadjoint orthogonal decomposition by $e_
u$ makes the standard weight space orthogonal to every other weight space, so [F4] gives $\sum_{s>0}\dim_Fe_
u\Delta_F(\lambda)^s=V(\det G_{\lambda
u})$. By [F2] and additivity of the valuation this is the sum over type-$
u$ semistandard $T$ of the valuations of their explicit monic norms; empty weight spaces use determinant $1$ and contribute $0$. [F2, F4, step 1.1]

The beta form of the hook side. Pad the beta lists to $N>n$. Removing a hook of length $h$ lowers one beta bead by $h$ with sorting sign $(-1)^{\operatorname{leg}}$, and adding it raises a bead by $h$ with the corresponding sign; the foot content is the lowered bead position minus $N$ plus $1$, up to the unit foot-residue shift. Thus the full signed equal-length hook side is precisely the finite shifted-beta Jacobi–Trudi polynomial: same-component inward ranges, crosscomponent earlier-to-later ranges, occupied-position zero terms and the unit shift are all covered by [F3]. Its coefficient at $\nu$ is $\sum_\mu J_{\lambda\mu}K_{\mu\nu}$. [F3, step 1.2]

Telescoping the marked-strip commutator. Apply the complete local identity [F3] to the product of successive type-row $\Gamma$ matrices and telescope $J\Gamma-\Gamma J$, starting from the empty shape where $J_0=0$. Each commutator inserts exactly the valuation of the strip factor at that label position, while all other $\Gamma$ factors retain the same tableau chain; summing the inserted positions gives the total valuation of the product of the factors over the chain, hence of the monic norm by [F2] and [F3]. The left endpoint of the telescope is exactly the auxiliary polynomial of step 2.2, so at the actual multipartition coefficient $
u$, $
u_\pi(\det G_{\lambda
u})=\sum_\mu J_{\lambda\mu}K_{\mu
u}$. Every auxiliary rank keeps the final-rank-$n$ parameters $U_a=Q_at^{na}$, with no rank-dependent deformation substituted during the telescope. [F2, F3, step 2.2]

Exactness of the valuations. For a nonzero difference $At^u-Bt^v$, unequal constants give valuation $0$, and equal constants with $u-v\ne0$ give valuation $1$ in characteristic zero or $p^{v_p(|u-v|)}$ in characteristic $p$ by [F5]. Artificial padded symbols in the crosscomponent minor proofs cancel formally before evaluation, and the retained terms are actual valid hook or node pairs whose exponent bound makes their differences nonzero in $K$; hence step 3.1 is valid over every $F$ and retains the higher positive-characteristic multiplicities. [F3, F5, step 3.1]

The integer Grothendieck class identity. Combining steps 2.1 and 3.1 shows that the actual multipartition-weight character of $\sum_{s>0}[\Delta_F(\lambda)^s]$ equals that of $\sum_\mu J_{\lambda\mu}[\Delta_F(\mu)]$. Weight projection is exact, so these are additive characters on the integer $K_0$ group [F4], and the standard classes form its $\mathbb Z$-basis by [F1]; their multipartition-weight matrix is unitriangular, hence invertible over $\mathbb Z$. A zero difference of weight characters therefore has all standard coefficients zero, which proves the asserted integer $K_0$ equality, with no rationalization and no Schur-functor injectivity claim. [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

proof_steps.text: Standard classes form a $\mathbb Z$-basis. The matrix of standard classes to simple classes is triangular with diagonal one by [F1], hence [F4] makes the classes $[\Delta(\lambda)]$ a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the integer Grothendieck group of the Schur cover, and the classes of the block projections are independent as well. [F1, F4]

Nonzero $J$-coefficients link the same block. Suppose $J_{\lambda\mu}\ne0$ and project the Jantzen sum identity of [F2] to all blocks other than the block of $\Delta(\lambda)$. Its left side is zero because each $\Delta_F(\lambda)^i$ is a submodule of the block-pure standard $\Delta(\lambda)$; its right side is a $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of standard classes lying in those other blocks, and the coefficient of $[\Delta(\mu)]$ in it is exactly $J_{\lambda\mu}\ne0$. Basis independence from step 1.1 forces that coefficient to vanish, a contradiction unless $\Delta(\mu)$ lies in the block of $\Delta(\lambda)$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

Blocks and Hecke linkage. By [F1], two standards share a Schur block exactly when they are linked by a finite chain of standards whose neighbouring terms share a simple factor. Step 2.2 converts each such shared factor into a $J$-edge to the common index, and step 2.1 shows every $J$-edge lies inside one block; hence sharing a Schur block is equivalent to $\sim_J$-connectivity. Applying the established Schur/Specht block correspondence of [F1] transfers this equivalence to the Murphy Specht modules and the Hecke algebra. In rank $0$ there is one empty standard, all positive filtration terms vanish, and the single empty class is its own Jantzen class; the argument never reduces $J$ coefficients modulo the field characteristic. proof_steps.text: One component at a time, at level one. Suppose first that the component sizes agree. For a single component $a$ of rank $m$, the actual level-one Hecke algebra is the finite Hecke algebra by [F3]. Its same-core Specht-block clause [F4], together with the level-one case of the Jantzen linkage equivalence [F1], connects any two rank-$m$ partitions with equal $e$-core by level-one Jantzen edges. The exact signed-conjugate bridge is $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)\cong P(\lambda^{\mathsf T})^\theta$, where $\theta(T_i)=-zT_i^{-1}$ and $P$ denotes the ordinary Dipper–James Specht module. If $\lambda,\mu$ have equal $e$-cores, their transposes have the equal transposed cores, so [F4] puts $P(\lambda^{\mathsf T})$ and $P(\mu^{\mathsf T})$ in the same ordinary Hecke block. An algebra automorphism sends primitive central idempotents bijectively to primitive central idempotents; its exact module pullback therefore preserves the equivalence of sharing a block. Applying the SAME $\theta$ to both modules gives the required Murphy block equality and then [F1] gives the level-one Jantzen connection. No untwisted conjugate-dual identity or algebraic-closure assumption is used. The rank $m=0$ case has a single empty partition and needs no block theorem. [F1, F3, F4, F5, F6]

Equalizing the component weights. If the component weights differ, choose a component whose weight exceeds its target and one whose weight is deficient; a positive-weight component has a removable $e$-hook by its core construction [F5]. For any prescribed foot residue $f$, moving the lowest bead on runner $f-1$ down by $e$ creates an $e$-hook with that foot residue, since its foot residue is the starting beta position plus one; wrap this hook in the deficient component with the same foot residue. The changed components determine the removed and added hook pair uniquely, and in the appropriate dominance orientation their $J$ contribution is one signed valuation with no cancellation; equal foot residues mean the nonzero generic difference is divisible by $t-1$, so the valuation is a positive integer. Nonzero generic foot differences are part of the exact formula [F2], and no unit-difference or characteristic-zero restriction is inserted. Thus the transfer is a Jantzen edge; it lowers the sum of squares of the discrepancies of the component hook weights by at least $2$, so finitely many such transfers equalize the component weights. Every $B$-linear map $B\to D_{01}$ is determined by the image of $1$, so $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{01},D_{01})=1$. [given, algebra]

**The symmetric form on $B$ and self-duality.** The coefficient functional $\tau(a+bx)=b$ is a symmetrizing trace on $B$: it is linear, $\tau(uv)=\tau(vu)$ for all $u,v$ (both sides pick out the $x$-coefficient of the product), and its radical is zero because $\tau(x)\ne0$, so the associated form $\langle u,v\rangle=\tau(uv)$ has matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ in the basis $(1,x)$, which is nonsingular. The anti-involution $\ast$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] that fixes $x$ is the identity of $B$ here, so the form is generator-fixing, and it exhibits an isomorphism $Y_{01}\cong Y_{01}^{\circledast}$: the dual of the regular module with respect to the trace. This is the actual symmetric-algebra proof of cover self-duality, not an inference from self-duality of the head. [step 1.1, given, algebra]

Each factor is generated by its images of $x,u$, so the homomorphism is onto the eight-dimensional product; the eight-word spanning bound proves that the span of the eight words is isomorphic to $M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus B_+\oplus B_-$ with $B_\pm=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$. The supported content cut at $2\alpha_0$ keeps the factor $M_2(\mathbb C)$; its simple module $\mathbb C^2$ has Gram matrix $J$, since $N^{t}J=JN$ and $(-J)^{t}J=J(-J)$, and it is self-dual and projective, so its projective cover is itself and its endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$; degree $0$ contributes $\mathbb C$, and Hom-spaces between distinct content blocks vanish because they are different blocks. In particular the one-dimensional Fock weight vector $M_{11}$ is not the two-dimensional module $D_{11}$, and the degree-two projective cover has vector-space dimension $2$ and composition length $1$. Higher supported degrees vanish directly: in an all-zero-residue module on at least three strands, restriction to strands $1,2$ forces $x_2=-x_1$ and $x_1^2=0$ by the matrix factor. Projection along this line gives $D_{01}=\pi M_{01}=\tfrac12(M_{01}+M_{10})$ and fixes the endpoints.
